Smoothed Empirical Hazard with Fitted Hazards

Source: R/plot_hazard_fits.R
plot_hazard_fits.Rd

Plots the smoothed empirical hazard (estimate_empirical_hazard) with the hazards of fitted parametric or spline models, extrapolated to a time horizon. As in plot_survival_fits, either one arm with one or more models (the empirical hazard black, each model with its colour and its AIC in the legend) or one model with one or more arms (each arm with its colour, the empirical hazard solid and the model dashed). The empirical hazard ends at the largest observed time of each arm, and the axes start at (0, 0). For the empirical hazard alone, use plot_empirical_hazard.

Usage

plot_hazard_fits(
  x,
  models = NULL,
  arms = NULL,
  fit_type = c("independent", "dependent"),
  conf_int = FALSE,
  time_horizon = NULL,
  y_max = NULL,
  y_label = "Hazard rate",
  break_by = NULL,
  n_points = 200,
  n_sim = 1000,
  seed = 1,
  legend_position = c("bottom", "right", "top", "left", "none"),
  colours = NULL,
  linetypes = NULL,
  text_sizes = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Object returned by fit_survival_models.

models

NULL (the default, all fitted models of fit_type) or model labels as in x$models$model, for example c("Weibull", "Hazards, 2 knots").

arms

NULL (the default, all arms) or the arms to plot.

fit_type

"independent" (the default, the model fitted to each arm) or "dependent" (the model fitted to both arms with the arm as a covariate).

conf_int

Logical; TRUE adds confidence bands (see Details). The default is FALSE.

time_horizon

NULL (the default, the largest observed time of the plotted arms) or the largest time of the plot, to show the extrapolation.

y_max

NULL (the default, see Details) or the upper limit of the y axis.

y_label

Label of the y axis. The default is "Hazard rate".

break_by

NULL (the default) or the spacing of the breaks of the time axis.

n_points

Number of times from 0 to the time horizon at which the models are evaluated. The default is 200.

n_sim

Number of simulated parameter vectors for the confidence band of a model. The default is 1000.

seed

Seed of the simulation. The default is 1.

legend_position

Position of the legend: "bottom" (the default), "right", "top", "left" or "none". Below or above the plot, the curves of one arm with several models are listed in two columns.

colours

NULL (the default colours) or colours of the curves. With one arm, the curves are the smoothed empirical hazard (named "Smoothed empirical hazard", black by default) and the models (named by their labels, as in models); with several arms, the curves are named by arm. A named vector sets the colours of the curves it names; an unnamed vector gives one colour per curve, in the order of the legend. With one arm, the confidence band of the model takes its colour; with several arms, the bands take the colours of the arms.

linetypes

NULL (the default) or line types of the smoothed empirical hazard ("Smoothed empirical hazard") and of the models (named by their labels), in both layouts, given as for colours (see plot_km for the line types). By default the lines are solid, except that of the model with several arms (dashed).

text_sizes

NULL (the default) or a named vector of font sizes in points, with some or all of the names "title" (titles of the plot and of its panels), "axis_title", "axis_text", "legend" and "risk_table" (numbers at risk and names of the arms below the plot; the title of the table is 1.125 times as large). The texts not named keep their default sizes: 14 points for the axis titles, 16.8 for the title of a plot, and 11.2 for the titles of panels, the axis text, the legend and the numbers at risk.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The hazards of the models are evaluated at n_points times from time_horizon / n_points to time_horizon (not at time 0, where some hazards are infinite). By default the y axis goes up to 1.2 times the largest of the empirical hazard (and its upper confidence limit with conf_int = TRUE) and of the model hazards after 5\ the time horizon, so that the very large hazards of some models just after time 0 do not set the scale. With conf_int = TRUE the confidence bands of the empirical hazards are drawn, and, when one model is plotted, the confidence band of the model simulated as in predict_survival.

Examples

dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
fits <- fit_survival_models(dat, distributions = c("exp", "weibull",
                                                   "llogis"),
                            spline_scales = NULL)
plot_hazard_fits(fits, arms = "Control", conf_int = TRUE)
